text: Every named STEP REST API call this app is coded to use -- route template, input, and what it returns -- so the app never hardcodes a STEP URL inline.
Every row is actually called somewhere in the codebase; every STEP call the codebase makes has a row here; each route resolves correctly against the real, live STEP server.
The canonical 66-book Bible ordering (book code + ordinal), the single source every book-order-dependent report/index reads instead of hardcoding it.
Exactly 66 rows, ordinals form an unbroken 0-65 sequence with no duplicates, and every book code matches a real live verse.osisId prefix in both directions.
The live STEP servers connection details (base_url, tagged version, timeout) -- so the app never hardcodes where/how it talks to STEP.
Every key is actually read (stepapi.py); the values genuinely work against the real, currently-running STEP server.
Folder/file patterns to exclude from content-index builds -- so a saturating file (e.g. generated prose) does not swamp search results with noise.
Every pattern actually corresponds to a real, still-relevant reason to exclude; correctly matches content_index own dormant/active state.
Per-pattern size-limit overrides for content-index builds, for files that legitimately need a different cap than the default.
Any row present corresponds to a real, still-needed override; 0 rows is correct when content_index itself is dormant.
Small bookkeeping table about the config store itself -- its version label and which database it describes.

config_version is genuinely read (Cfg.config_version, the live fingerprint mechanism); every key present is actually consumed somewhere -- found live 2026-08-30: the database key is not, a minor orphan.
Strong-number accept/reject/synonym rules for the (now retired) candidate-discovery system.
Consistent with its documented retirement -- all rows correctly inactive, matching retract_candidate_system.py; not a live input to anything.
Every generic secondary SQLite index this app declares for its data tables -- table+column set the builder must create.
Every registered index actually exists live with matching columns; every table it names is real; found+fixed live 2026-08-30: escalation_history was missing its registered index entirely.
Per step+condition, what path (ok/pause/stop/etc) a run takes on that outcome, and what message to show -- so failure routing is data, not a hardcoded if/elif chain.
Every active row names a real active step; every path value is a real member of the path vocabulary; inactive rows correspond to conditions the code genuinely no longer produces.
The canonical controlled-vocabulary registry -- every fixed set of allowed values project-wide, one source of truth instead of scattered hardcoded lists.

Every group is actually enforced against live data somewhere, and every group defined here is actually consulted -- verified via the existing find_enum_violations check, zero violations across the whole dataset.

The rulebook for how the escalation system itself must behave (source classification, duplicate suppression, module-blocking, documentation-followup obligations), each rule honestly stating whether it is mechanically enforced or session practice.

Every rule claiming mechanical enforcement is actually enforced by the code it names -- found+fixed live 2026-08-30: module_blocking claimed active/wired but the gate was genuinely commented out since escalation #859.
The field-level enforcement engine behind cfg_escalations policies -- what is required on each escalation action (comment at raise, resolution at approval, etc).
Every rules claimed check genuinely fires -- 5 of 10 rows empirically triggered and confirmed working correctly the same session this was reviewed, not just read from code.

THE schema definition for every data table in the app -- column name/type/constraints/FK/expected-enum, read by build_data_tables() to physically create tables and by Db.write() to validate every write.
Every column here matches the live physical schema exactly, in both directions -- confirmed live 2026-08-30 via find_unregistered_tables_and_columns, now 0 drift after fixing 26 rows.
Composite natural-key definitions for tables whose dedup key is more than one column -- read by table_ddl()/Db.upsert() to know what counts as the same row.

Every registered composite key matches a real live unique index; a table with a genuine composite PK must use THIS table, never repeated is_pk=1 flags -- found+fixed live 2026-08-30 (content_index had exactly this mistake).
The state-machine rules for how an escalations next_action+conditions resolve to its actual state -- config-driven instead of a hardcoded if/elif chain.

Every priority/condition/resulting-status combination genuinely fires correctly for real transactions -- confirmed live 2026-08-30 (the needs_claude_followup fix, tested end-to-end, 6/6 passing both directions).
Documents which status values an entity (escalation, prose_section, word) can hold and what sets each one -- a reference table for _status_for()s substring lookup, not itself the primary mechanism.

Every status genuinely reachable that _status_for() actually resolves to is described here -- found+fixed live 2026-08-30 (extended the re-assigned rows set_by text to also cover the new needs_claude_followup case).
